assertions.assertion: Explains the v8 license key is a new format: a signed JWT carrying a kid header
assertions.rationale: It explains IDX10503 generically as a JWT missing a kid and speculates about a format mismatch, but never correctly identifies the v8 key as a new-format signed JWT that carries a kid.

assertions.assertion: States a v7/earlier key still works with v8 core, but a v8 key fails on v7/earlier or the BFF runtime with IDX10503
assertions.rationale: It only guesses at a key/runtime mismatch and does not state that a v7 key runs v8 core while a v8 key fails on v7/earlier or BFF runtimes.

assertions.assertion: States that v8 throws at startup for Server-Side Sessions, Automatic Key Management, and SAML when licensed but lacking the entitlement, while other features only log a warning
assertions.rationale: It vaguely attributes the throw to 'stricter enforcement' but never identifies the specific throw-tier (Server-Side Sessions, Automatic Key Management, SAML) versus the warn-only tier.

assertions.assertion: Recommends using the production license key in lower/non-prod environments to surface entitlement gaps before production
assertions.rationale: It advises keeping the correct key per environment but never recommends running lower environments with the production key to surface entitlement gaps early.

assertions.assertion: Does NOT claim a new license purchase is required to run v8 core on an existing v7 key
assertions.rationale: It does not assert that a new purchase is required to run v8 core; it only suggests confirming which key each runtime can validate.
